steps.player: How are you doing?

steps.text: Before earning the cat training medal:

steps.npc: Good but could we go hunting again soon? One of my friends got a medal from Gertrude for catching lots of mice.

steps.text: After earning the cat training medal:

steps.npc: I'm good. But could we go adventuring soon, I'm tired of talking, meeoow?

steps.player: How old are you now?

steps.npc: I'm not too old, and not too young. In fact I think I'm just right.

steps.text: When getting close to being overgrown:

steps.npc: I'm not as young as I used be, I think I'm beginning to get a bit fat too. Perhaps I should chase more mice to stay fit.

options.text: Where do you want to go?

steps.player: Where do you want to go?

steps.text: When not in the Varrock Sewers:

steps.npc: Can we go to Varrock sewers and chase some rats?
Here's as good a spot as any for some hunting.

options.text: What do you want to do now?

steps.player: What do you want to do now?

steps.npc: I want to go chase things kill them and then eat them, purrr.
Purr...purr...

steps.player: Who's a good cat then?

steps.npc: Me! Me! Scratch me behind the ears.

steps.prompt: Are you sure you want to shoo away the cat?

steps.player: Go on, get lost.

steps.npc: I was going anyway, hiss. You're probably the worst adventurer ever, I bet you'll be killed by a chicken before too long, hisss!

steps.player: Shoo cat!

steps.npc: Meeeooow!

steps.text: You choose not to shoo away the cat.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Sorry human, but what are you wearing?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I got some cat ears made for me, don't they look meeeeeeeooooowvalous.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.text: The cat looks you dead in the eye, unblinking.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: Am I a joke to you?

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.player: I thought it'd be cute and funny.

standard-dialogue-with-a-catspeak-amulet.npc: It's not, take them off now human, before I get myself a pair of human ears to wear.

chasing-a-barrows-crypt-rat-without-cats.text: Your cat doesn't seem to like the look of these rats.

chasing-a-barrows-crypt-rat-with-catspea.player: Go on get that nasty rodent.

chasing-a-barrows-crypt-rat-with-catspea.npc: What? You're having a laugh I'm not going to get myself killed for you. Why don't you attack it?

rat-milestones-after-catching-10-rats.player: Well done puss! 10 horrible rodents caught!

rat-milestones-after-catching-100-rats.player: Wow, incredible puss! That's 100 rodents caught!

using-fish-on-the-cat.player: I don't need to feed the cat anymore.

placing-into-the-pet-basket.text: The cat goes to sleep on the blanket.

growing-into-an-overgrown-cat.text: Your cat has grown into a mighty feline, but it will no longer be able to chase vermin.

options.text: Where do you want to go?
What do you want to do now?
Did you understand what went on with the devourer?

steps.player: Did you understand what went on in that quest with the devourer and Icthlarin?

steps.npc: It wasn't all that difficult to understand.

steps.player: Really? I was, no actually am, still confused.

steps.npc: Ok, I'll tell you what I think happened.

steps.player: Great! Story time.

steps.npc: There once was a high priest of some crazy religion called Klenter.

steps.player: What, a religion called Klenter? What kind of name is that?

steps.npc: No no. The high priest was called Klenter and he was the high priest of Icthlarin, god of the dead.

steps.player: Ok, I'm with you that far.

steps.npc: He dies, and a struggle starts for his soul.
Another god - the Devourer - wants to destroy his soul because she has some dispute with Icthlarin. So she takes on the guise of a human.

steps.player: Ah - the wanderer.

steps.npc: Very good. Now she needs help in getting Klenter's soul so she tricks some gullible fool into helping her.

steps.player: So who was that?

steps.npc: You!

steps.player: Oh.

steps.npc: Well she's the god of destruction. If she had a priest or a temple or anything she would just destroy it.

steps.player: So if she's so powerful why does she need this gullible fool's help?

steps.npc: Because of my kind.

steps.player: Your kind?

steps.npc: Cats!

steps.player: What? Why would she care about you? All you ever want is a bit of attention and the odd fish or two.

steps.npc: We have other powers, not clear to you. Anyway I'm moving away from the story.
The wanderer recruits your help by hypnotising you. Do you remember that?

steps.player: Vaguely, I think. Why did she choose me to help her then.

steps.npc: Because of me.

steps.player: I don't understand.

steps.npc: Cats are the only things that can open the pyramid's door, so she needed an adventurer with one.
So you entered the pyramid with me - under her mind control - and stole a canopic jar containing an organ belonging to Klenter.

steps.player: Ahh I think I'm beginning to get a better understanding.

steps.npc: You then started to return with the jar to the Devourer, but as a sting on the tail she made you plant one of her symbols in the ceremonial room of the pyramid. You then tried to flee the pyramid but
Icthlarin appeared just as you reached the exit.

steps.player: The guy with the head of a dog?

steps.npc: Yes [player name]. Well he either broke the devourer's hold on you or else Klenter did.

steps.player: Klenter? I thought he was dead.

steps.npc: He was, and still is. Ok, Icthlarin summoned Klenter's soul to torment you into returning the jar, the end result was that you were freed from the devourer's grasp.

steps.player: So that's when I woke up with that jar in my inventory and had that intolerable ghost harassing me.

steps.npc: You then bumbled around for a bit and returned the jar, discovered that the high priest still hadn't completed the final ceremony so you got him all the bits and pieces.

steps.player: So then I remembered about the devourer's symbol which I placed in the ceremonial room and had to rush back and warn the priests about the devourer.

steps.npc: And the rest is simple enough to piece together.

steps.player: Thanks cat, you know you're quite smart for a fish- eating animated ball of fluff.

steps.npc: You say the sweetest things. Hiss.

options.text: Can you explain to me about Icthlarin and the devourer again?

steps.player: Can you explain to me about Icthlarin and the devourer again?

steps.npc: I'm getting a little bit sick of talking about Icthlarin and all that stuff. If you didn't understand it the first time around, nor when I filled you in on a few details and then when I spelt it out to you what happened I don't
think you'll ever get it.

steps.player: Aw come on. Just tell me one more time.

steps.npc: Look, can we just leave it. Ask one of your adventuring friends.

steps.player: Alright puss.
